$comment: BareCount AWS naming & tagging registry — implementation contract for the CDK guardrail Aspect. Governed by ADR DEC-e39ed3. Versioned by filename; amendments bump the version (v2, ...). Every governed resource type is in exactly ONE of the three classes below; a type in none fails synth closed (must be classified).
$classes: Every governed resource type MUST appear in exactly one of: classA_nameable, classB_nonNameableTaggable, classC_nonNameableNonTaggable. The Aspect fails synth on any encountered type that is in none (forces a registry amendment).

classA_nameable.$comment: has a configurable physical-name property; the property MUST equal the convention name; carries requiredTags

classB_nonNameableTaggable.$comment: CloudFormation names it; no useful name property, but IS taggable — identified by its Name tag (= convention name) + carries requiredTags

identityMapping.AWS::KMS::Key: identified by its companion AWS::KMS::Alias (alias/{base}-key, classA) plus a Name tag {base}-key

classC_nonNameableNonTaggable.$comment: structural glue or contract/tool-named resources: no convention-name property AND (not taggable OR named by a separate contract). Neither the name check nor the tag check applies. SSM::Parameter is governed by the SSM path contract (/bc/{stage}/{domain}); CDK::Metadata is tool-injected. Identity is the CFN logical id within its (already-conformant) stack.
classC_nonNameableNonTaggable.identityRule: identified by CDK construct path / CFN logical id within the stack; the Aspect asserts neither a physical name nor tags for these

globalNamespaceExceptions.$comment: namespaces global across ALL accounts; the classA name additionally appends the account id for uniqueness

$tagExempt: nameable (or taggable-class) types that do NOT support resource tags — the Aspect checks their name but skips the required-tags check. KMS aliases cannot carry tags.
